messages.content: I have the four combinations open now. Can you put them side by side for the three of us, including one checked suitcase each way? I care about the actual family total, not just the headline fare.

Yes. I’ll compare the two nonstop departures on Thursday, October 10, with the two nonstop returns on Monday, October 14. I’ll include the ticket restrictions, carry-ons, one shared checked bag in each direction, and the effect on usable time in New Orleans.
The outbound choices are American at 5:35 p.m. or Southwest at 9:15 a.m. The returns are American at 10:25 a.m. or Southwest at 5:50 p.m.

Using the fares currently displayed, the American flights are Basic Economy at $151 per person outbound and $139 per person returning. A standard carry-on is included, but the shared checked suitcase is $40 each way. Those tickets are nonchangeable, and cancellation would produce a credit only after the displayed $99-per-person deduction. Seat selection may cost extra.
And the Southwest terms? The fare page is not making the bag comparison very obvious.

The Southwest Wanna Get Away fares are $177 per person outbound and $181 per person returning. A carry-on is included, and the checkout display for these dates includes one checked bag per traveler, so your single suitcase adds nothing. Changes are allowed with any fare difference due; cancellation produces a nontransferable flight credit rather than a cash refund. The bag allowance should be rechecked on the final purchase screen because the policy shown must match the travel date.
What are the four totals, then?

American both ways is $950 for three tickets plus the suitcase. American outbound and Southwest return is $1,036. Southwest outbound and American return is $988. Southwest both ways is $1,074. Those totals exclude optional paid seat assignments but include the stated bag charge where applicable.
So the cheapest pair also gives us the least time there.

Correct. The $950 American pairing lands at 6:55 p.m. Thursday and departs at 10:25 a.m. Monday. After deplaning and the airport ride, hotel arrival would likely be around 8:00 p.m.; on Monday you would need to leave around 8:15 a.m. The trip effectively has three full days and little usable time on either end.
How much do the mixed choices improve that?

The $1,036 American-outbound/Southwest-return pairing keeps the late Thursday arrival but restores most of Monday, with an airport departure from the hotel around 3:45 p.m. The $988 Southwest-outbound/American-return pairing reaches New Orleans at 10:40 a.m. Thursday, allowing a bag drop and most of the afternoon, but Monday is still largely lost. The $1,074 Southwest pairing preserves both Thursday afternoon and most of Monday.
Tie that back to the two hotels. Does arriving early change the Warehouse versus Mid-City comparison?

It strengthens the Warehouse District option. With the 10:40 a.m. arrival, you can leave bags at The Higgins around noon and begin the museum area that afternoon without another cross-city ride. Mid-City remains slightly cheaper overall, but you would ride there to drop bags and then travel back toward the first-day attractions. With the 6:55 p.m. arrival, either hotel is mainly an arrival-and-dinner night, though Mid-City takes a little longer from the airport.
The all-Southwest schedule is only $124 more than the cheapest combination, right? And it still keeps the complete Higgins plan below $3,200?

Yes. It is $124 more than American both ways. With The Higgins, airport and local transportation, and the $350 activity allowance already used in the comparison, the complete estimate remains $2,823.40. That leaves $376.60 below the $3,200 ceiling.
